label: lem:compact_subset_open_collar
title: Compact subset of an open set has a positive collar
statement:
Let \(K,U \subset \C\). If \(K\) is compact, \(U\) is open, and \(K \subset U\),
    then there exists \(\rho > 0\) such that the open \(\rho\)-thickening of
    \(K\) is contained in \(U\):
    \[
      \mathrm{thickening}(\rho, K) \subset U .
    \]
    For nonempty \(K\) this thickening agrees with
    \(\{z \in \C : \dist(z,K) < \rho\}\); the formulation via
    \texttt{Metric.thickening} is preferred because it also handles the empty
    case correctly (where \texttt{Metric.thickening}\(\,\rho\,\emptyset = \emptyset\)).
proof:
Since \(K\) is compact and \(U^c\) is closed, and since \(K \cap U^c=\varnothing\),
    the distance between \(K\) and \(U^c\) is positive. Choose \(\rho\) smaller than
    this distance. (In Mathlib this is essentially
    \texttt{IsCompact.exists\_thickening\_subset\_open}.)
notes: Signature: `lemma compact_subset_open_has_thickening {K U : Set ℂ} (hK : IsCompact K) (hU : IsOpen U) (hKU : K ⊆ U) : ∃ ρ > 0, Metric.thickening ρ K ⊆ U`. Originally formulated with `{z : ℂ | Metric.infDist z K < ρ} ⊆ U`, but that form is false in the corner case K = U = ∅ (since `Metric.infDist _ ∅ = 0`). Reformulated using `Metric.thickening` (which uses `infEDist`, equal to ∞ on ∅, so `Metric.thickening ρ ∅ = ∅`). For nonempty K the two formulations are equivalent. Direct one-liner from `IsCompact.exists_thickening_subset_open`.
